All 16 views complete. Summary of analysis:

- **Test image**: Tomato stem at soil line, white/grayish mycelial mat coating the lower stem with small dark sclerotia (black dots) visible, bleached stem tissue, black plastic mulch in background.

- **Southern_Blight** - Best match: white mycelial growth at soil line with small sclerotia characteristic of *Sclerotium rolfsii*. The reference images show identical presentation.

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** - Has white mycelium but much larger sclerotia (~1cm vs the small dots in the test image). Not as close.

- All other classes (leaf diseases, bacterial wilts, fruit rots) do not match the stem/soil-line white mycelium + small sclerotia pattern seen in the test image.

The small round sclerotia (mustard-seed sized) combined with the white silky mycelial mat at the crown/soil interface is the hallmark signature of Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii). The plastic mulch background is also consistent with this high-value crop setting where Southern Blight is common.
